title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (H2 2026)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), design principles, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference initiative that unifies hosting, dedicated, and private deployments under a single developer experience. It is intended for product, engineering, GTM, and customer-facing teams.

Scope: Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Console observability, and Optimize cost/performance controls as they relate to a consistent API and rollout strategy.

1) Executive summary

- Goal: Deliver a single, opinionated developer interface and rollout path for customers to move seamlessly between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private inference with predictable latency and cost controls.
- Success metrics (OKRs):
  - Platform adoption: +30% q/q in active projects migrating from ad-hoc self-host to Redwood Dedicated/private in 6 months.
  - Latency SLOs: 99th percentile token latency <= 250ms for common conversational models on Dedicated with burst enabled.
  - Unit economics: 15-25% reduction in per-token cost for cached/batched workloads using Optimize recommendations.

2) Product requirements (PRD)

2.1 Core requirements (must-have)
- Unified API: Single REST/SDK surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Versioned models & pinning: Customers must be able to pin model version and rollout policy per route.
- Smart routing: Policy-based routing (latency, cost, region, tier) with automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Observability: Token-level cost and latency breakdown per request and per-route dashboards.
- Migration tooling: One-click config export/import and recommended instance profiles for Dedicated/private installs.

2.2 Important non-functional requirements
- Security: Support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated, audit logging for all control-plane actions.
- Performance: Serving runtime must support continuous batching, KV cache sharing, and quantization variants with negligible correctness regressions.
- Reliability: Canary rollout and automatic fallback with configurable thresholds.

2.3 Acceptance criteria
- End-to-end: A test application can be deployed to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with identical SDK calls and demonstrate equivalent behavior across deployments.
- SLOs: Metrics pipeline surfaces 99th/95th/50th token latency and cost per 1M tokens.
- Security: KMS-based encryption verified in Private environment penetration checklist.

3) Design specs & architecture overview

3.1 High-level flow
- API Gateway -> Route Router (policy engine) -> Model Selection -> Serving Runtime -> Telemetry & Billing

3.2 Key components and responsibilities
- Route Router: Evaluates routing policy and selects candidate model variants. Supports weighted canaries and failover rules.
- Serving Runtime: Kernel selection, quantization paths, prefix/KV cache and continuous batching.
- Telemetry: Token-level traces, per-route cost attributions, and drift detectors for quality regressions.
- Control Plane: Model catalog, versioning, rollout manager, and private deployment connectors.

3.3 Data contracts and APIs
- Model Catalog API: /v1/models (list), /v1/models/{id}/versions (list), /v1/models/{id}/promote (POST)
- Route config (YAML example):
  route: customer-chat
  model: redwood/gpt-rlhf-1
  version: v2026-02-14
  routing_policy:
    priority: [latency, cost]
    canary: {percent: 5, version: v2026-03-01}

3.4 Rollout & fallback behavior (numbered steps)
1. Create route and pin stable model version.
2. Enable canary with 5% traffic to a new variant.
3. Observe latency, error-rate, and quality (eval set) for 24 hours.
4. If thresholds exceeded, auto-roll back to previous stable version and notify owners.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters)

Theme A — Unified runtime parity (Q2–Q3 2026)
- Deliver feature parity in Serving Runtime across Hosted and Dedicated for quantization and KV cache sharing.
- Milestone: Dedicated supports same kernel selection heuristics by end of Q3.

Theme B — Migration & Developer experience (Q3–Q4 2026)
- One-click migration templates, SDK improvements, and sample apps for common workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings).
- Milestone: Migration templates published and featured in Console by early Q4.

Theme C — Cost controls & Optimize integration (Q4 2026 – Q1 2027)
- Deep integration with Redwood Optimize for automated batching, cache hints, and quantization recommendations by workload.
- Milestone: Auto-tune pilot for 3 enterprise customers in Q1 2027.

Theme D — Enterprise readiness (Q1–Q2 2027)
- Harden Private deployment UX, on-prem packaging, and compliance evidence bundles (SOC2/ISO).
- Milestone: Private 1.0 on-prem package and legal/compliance playbook.

5) Pricing & packaging guidance

5.1 Hosted (Redwood API)
- Consumption pricing continues: per-token generation + per-embedding unit.
- New network-tiered pricing: Standard and SLO-backed Premium (Premium includes 99.9% uptime SLA and lower request throttling).

5.2 Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Base: monthly committed GPU-hours + per-token runtime surcharge.
- Add-on: Burst capacity (pay-as-you-go) and prioritized routing.
- Discounting guidance: 10-20% off Hosted list for 12-month commitments; 20-35% for 36-months depending on capacity tier.

5.3 Private (VPC/on-prem)
- License fee: platform + deployment support.
- Optional: managed upgrades & extended observability retention as add-ons.

Packaging examples (recommended tiers)
- Developer: small Hosted with higher per-token unit; ideal for proof-of-concepts.
- Production: Dedicated 1-4 clusters, priority routing, baseline support.
- Enterprise: Private + Dedicated hybrid, premium SLAs, & compliance add-ons.

6) Release notes (current release: 2026-03)

Summary: This release publishes the Unified Inference PRD baseline, initial Route Router prototype, and Console migration templates (beta).

Notable changes:
- Feature: Route Router v0 — supports policy evaluation and weighted canaries.
- Feature: Console migration templates — import/export route configs and recommended instance profiles.
- Improvement: Telemetry pipeline adds token-level cost attribution and per-route latency breakdown.
- Bugfix: Fixed incorrect cache invalidation during model version swaps on Dedicated clusters.

Known limitations and mitigations:
- Limitation: Private on-prem package does not yet include automated kernel selection for quantized models. Mitigation: manual kernel hinting in deployment spec (documented).
- Limitation: Optimize integration for auto-tuning is in pilot; customers should follow the manual recommendation baseline.

Release checklist (table):
- [ ] Docs: PRD and migration guides published in Console docs.
- [ ] Security: KMS integration verification completed for two pilot customers.
- [ ] SRE: Load test at 1.5x expected peak for Dedicated.
- [ ] Sales enablement: Pricing guidance and playbook updated for AE use.

- Engineering leads: Mateo Ruiz (serving runtime), Elena Park (control plane & console).
- SRE/ops: Priya Shah.
- Next steps (30/60/90):

  - 60 days: complete Dedicated parity items for kernel selection and cache sharing.
  - 90 days: begin Optimize auto-tune pilot with 3 customers.
